title: Delineating Oxidation Aspects of an Additively Manufactured Nanoprecipitation-Strengthened Al<sub>0.2</sub>Co<sub>1.5</sub>CrFeNi<sub>1.5</sub>Ti<sub>0.3</sub> High-Entropy Alloy.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: pre-alloyed gas-atomized powder of the equiatomic high-entropy alloy composition Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3, mean particle size ~30 µm
recollection.intervention: Guess: laser powder‐bed fusion (LPBF) to build bulk specimens, followed by an aging heat treatment (e.g. 700 °C for 4 h) to precipitate strengthening phases
recollection.structure: Guess: a primarily face‐centered‐cubic (FCC) matrix with nanoscale L12 or B2‐ordered Al–Ti‐rich precipitates (~5–20 nm) dispersed uniformly
recollection.mechanism: Guess: oxidation resistance derives from selective outward diffusion of Al and Ti to form a continuous Al2O3-rich surface scale; nanoprecipitates refine grain size and slow oxygen ingress by grain‐boundary pinning
recollection.results: Guess: at 800 °C in air, the alloy exhibited a parabolic oxidation rate constant ~2×10^–12 kg^2/m^4·s, oxide‐scale thickness ~5 µm after 100 h, and maintained matrix hardness ~450 HV and yield strength ~1 GPa after long‐term exposure

score.note: Correctly inferred additive manufacturing followed by aging, but the proposed 700°C/4 h treatment differs from the actual 750°C/50 h treatment. The FCC matrix and nanoscale L12-type precipitation are partly correct, though the actual aged structure included both Ni/Ti-rich L12 and Al/Ti-rich L21 precipitates. The mechanism is wrong: protection arose mainly from a continuous Cr2O3-rich scale, not continuous Al2O3 formed by Al/Ti diffusion or grain-boundary pinning. None of the stated oxidation, scale-thickness, hardness, or strength values match the reported results.
